s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological and systemic symptoms with signs of infection and inflammation
salient_findings: Progressive headache, phonophobia, high-grade fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea
Nuchal rigidity without focal neurologic deficits
key_facts: 44-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Recent treatment for SLE-associated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Presented with a one-week history of progressive headache and fever
Had hemoglobin of 11.2 g/dL, eosinophils 150 cells/mm3, and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL
Lumbar puncture revealed low glucose, high protein, and 42 white cells/mm3
Cerebrospinal fluid culture grew Enterococcus gallinarum
Developed hemoptysis, bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates, and acute respiratory failure
Required mechanical ventilation and ICU admission
Developed a purpuric skin rash on hospital day 4
